sources.entry: Shell: _Docker implemented in around 100 lines of bash_

summary.one_liner: Bocker is a minimal Docker-like container tool written in roughly 100 lines of bash.
summary.what_it_does: Bocker implements a subset of Docker's commands in bash: pulling images, listing images and containers, running commands in containers, viewing logs, committing containers to new images, and removing containers and images. It stores images and containers on a btrfs filesystem mounted at /var/bocker. It sets up networking through a bridge called bridge0 with iptables routing, and applies CPU share and memory limits through cgroups, configurable via BOCKER_CPU_SHARE and BOCKER_MEM_LIMIT. A limited "bocker init" command provides a basic version of docker build. Data volumes, volume containers, and port forwarding are not implemented.
use_cases: learning how containers work under the hood
running isolated commands in a bash-based container
experimenting with btrfs snapshots for container images
setting up container networking with a bridge and iptables
applying cgroup CPU and memory limits to test processes
how_to_run: Install prerequisites: btrfs-progs, curl, iproute2, iptables, libcgroup-tools, util-linux >= 2.25.2, coreutils >= 7.5
Create network bridge bridge0 with IP 10.0.0.1/24
Enable IP forwarding via /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward and route bridge0 traffic to a physical interface
Optionally use the included Vagrantfile to build the environment
Run commands such as: bocker pull centos 7, bocker images, bocker run img_ID cat /etc/centos-release
notable: Docker-style CLI implemented in about 100 lines of bash
Uses btrfs for image and container storage
Network bridge and iptables routing for container traffic
CPU share and memory limits via cgroups, set with environment variables
Includes a Vagrantfile to build a suitable test environment
caveats: README warns it runs as root and changes network interfaces, routing and firewall rules; the author makes no guarantee it won't break your system, so run it in a VM
Requires a specific system setup (btrfs mount, bridge0, IP forwarding, firewall rules) and a newer util-linux than most distributions ship
Port forwarding, data volumes, and volume containers are not implemented
bocker build is only a very limited version via bocker init
